Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers manager due to ill health.

The 62-year-old, who previously had to walk away from his job at Birmingham City in 2024 due to a battle with bowel cancer, leaves Blackburn with immediate effect.

The Championship side announced his departure with a statement from Mowbray. It read: 'Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role as Head Coach of Blackburn Rovers.

'I’m immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

'Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you’ve given me. It’s been a pleasure working alongside you.

In a recent development, 'To the fans, thank you for the way you’ve supported me and the team this season. I’ve always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers boss due to ill health.

'I’m grateful to the Owners and Suhail (Pasha, chief operating officer) for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

Recent findings suggest that 'I’d ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time. Thank you for your understanding.'.

Mowbray leaves with Blackburn 13th in the Championship. He took over at the club in June this year having spent two years out of the game following his health challenges at Birmingham City.

The veteran manager suddenly stepped down as manager of Birmingham in February 2024 after undergoing surgery for bowel cancer. He had 15cm of his bowel removed during his treatment.

He took a temporary leave of absence after eight games in charge, before officially resigning from the role in May.

Mowbray, who has managed a host of English clubs, opened up publicly about his struggles, telling the Times that his children had feared the worst.

'I had the conversation with my family and you could see they were frightened,' he stated. 'Was I frightened? My only thoughts were for my family, my three children and my wife and making sure they were OK.

In a recent development, 'I had to put everything in order and I tried to. My wife saw our banking app for the first time in her life. It's little things like that. She understood. This was serious stuff. I felt she needed to know where we had our money, whether it was ISAs or pensions and what was in the bank.'.

Recent findings suggest that speaking on his diagnosis, which came after he collapsed when trying to answer the door, he added: 'My wife put me in the car and drove me back to hospital and they wanted to know why I was collapsing and in the condition I was,' he notes. 'They rehydrated me and put me on a drip overnight.

Sources indicate that 'I remember sitting there in bed and my kids' eyes were watering up. They were scared I wasn't going to live. How old were they? They were 15, 17 and 19. I could see the fear in their eyes.'.

In a recent development, mowbray's comeback story when he was made Blackburn boss in the summer was one of the feel-good moments of the offseason. It has not been disclosed what his current health matter is.

Mowbray leaves Blackburn with the team in 13th place in the Championship table.

Blackburn Rovers owner Balaji Rao added his own statement, writing: 'Our thoughts are with Tony and his family as he steps back from his duties to focus on his health.

'Through our many meetings over the years, we’ve come to know Tony well and grown very fond of him. We’ve always admired his professionalism, his dedication and the passion he brings to his work at Blackburn Rovers.

According to recent reports, 'Tony, please know that you have our unconditional and unwavering support. We send you and your family our love and strength, and we will do all we can to support you through this time.'.

Chief Executive Officer Steve Curwood remarked: 'Tony’s passion for the club and his professionalism are clear to see, but it is his kindness and the care he indicates for players, staff and those around him that mean so much.

It has been revealed that 'Our priority now is to make sure he feels that same care and support from all of us. We will support him and his family in every way we can.

'On behalf of everyone at Blackburn Rovers, I would like to send Tony and his family our very best wishes during this time.'.

Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.
  • This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.
  • He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he remarked.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

Recent findings suggest that given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

Recent findings suggest that that was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a newly introduced manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

According to recent reports, moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

Playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

According to recent reports, there were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

Millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

Millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

Newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

So much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

Well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil mentioned: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

Industry observers note that “We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

Industry observers note that as for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

Sources indicate that the draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

It has been revealed that the third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:.

Crystal Palace 3-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-3 Bradford City.

From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

“I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” noted Willock after the match.

“100% [the competition is vital], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a latest coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a major game in keeping that momentum.”.

"We remarked at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT.

Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:.

According to recent reports, moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

Sources indicate that seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

Willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

It has been revealed that newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

Recent findings suggest that finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

You can hear the travelling fans now!

Sources indicate that marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

It has been revealed that issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

Recent findings suggest that millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

Industry observers note that double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

It has been revealed that free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

What colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

It’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

Newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

Sources indicate that scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Promising restart for the home side.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:.

Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here.

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

In a recent development, millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

It has been revealed that the game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

Industry observers note that the delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Industry observers note that newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

González is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

In a recent development, millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

Hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

According to recent reports, I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

First piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

Barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

Wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

Sources indicate that newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

Sources indicate that another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

Again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

Murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

It has been revealed that newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

Industry observers note that fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Just a reminder of the teams starting today:.

Starting XI: Filip Marschall; Jordi Osei-Tutu, Caleb Taylor, Jake Cooper, Elkan Baggott; Lyndon Dykes, Jenson Metcalfe; Camiel Neghli, Daniel Kelly, Romain Esse; Zak Lovelace.

Substitutes: Regan Monty, Tristan Parkes, Sacha Vieira, George Beaumont, Yanis Issoufou, George Evans, Taïryk Arconte, Alfie Massey, Zak Sturge.

Starting XI: Lukás Hornícek; Lewis Hall, Fabian Schär, Amar Dedic, Sven Botman; Jacob Murphy, Nico González; Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Joe Willock; Yoane Wissa.

Substitutes: Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga, Malick Thiaw, Nick Pope, Lewis Miley, Bazoumana Touré, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Aladji Bamba, Sean Steur.

Recent findings suggest that the teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

"We've tried to find the right balance" ⚖️Matthias Jaissle on his team selection for tonight's match with Millwall ⚫️ pic.twitter.com/kiRRxAgLk8.

We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

Recent findings suggest that alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach says has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

In a recent development, at the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.

You can read Luke Edwards’ full story on that here.

The Premier League teams playing in European competitions enter the EFL Cup in this round, with all 16 fixtures being played over five match days. As well as tonight’s games there will be:.

Peterborough United vs Barnsley (7.45pm).

Fleetwood Town vs Sheffield United (7.45pm).

Manchester City vs Norwich City (7.30pm).

*all kick-off at 8pm, unless stated otherwise.

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

Jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

It has been revealed that bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

Aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight upcoming signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

The visitors have arrived in south London.

We've made it to South East London 👋 pic.twitter.com/nh8Fpa37xT.

We’re bringing you the action from the pick of tonight’s EFL Cup games but there are also four games kicking off at 7.45pm:.

Crystal Palace vs Middlesbrough.

The Champions League also returns tonight and you can follow along with both our blogs:.

Aston Villa are currently 3-1 up against Club Brugge in Belgium – follow the action here.

Manchester City will face Porto at 8.00pm – our live blog has just gone live here with the team news from both sides.

Here is how the visitors are lining up:.

Yoane Wissa takes the captain’s armband tonight, while Jacob Ramsey starts up front after scoring a late equaliser against Bournemouth on Saturday.

Your Mags at Millwall ✊ pic.twitter.com/zfnHgTlWgh.

Here is your Millwall starting XI:.

Keeper Filip Marschall is making his debut while Jensen Metcalfe is back in the squad after his red card against Bolton was overturned on appeal.

How your Lions line-up tonight 🔢 pic.twitter.com/wEp6qLIz4Y.

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Industry observers note that newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the new season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:43 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 09:33 EST, 17 November 2026.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins issued a warning to her followers after learning that she had been being impersonated on social media.

The 26-year-old has over 58,000 followers on Instagram having built up a loyal fanbase via her work on broadcasters covering the top flight and NFL in the US.

But Collins was forced to make a statement after an imposter was found to have been reaching out to people in her name over a number of months.

'I want to make people aware that someone has been impersonating me on WhatsApp, messaging high-profile athletes, pretending to be me with their username set to my name and a picture of me,' she told her followers on the social media app.

'This has been happening on and off for several months and seems to be upping in frequency more recently.

'I have reported this to the police and they’ve asked that I share it on here to make people aware, particularly anyone I have worked with or connected with in the football/sports world.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins has warned fans of an impersonator pretending to be her on social media (All photos source: Instagram/Ellie Collins).

The 26-year-old maintains an active presence on the site and has over 58,000 followers.

After previously working as a waitress, Collins transitioned into broadcasting four years ago.

Since starting her career in the media, Collins has had the opportunity to interview a number of sports stars including Frank Lampard.

Industry observers note that 'If you receive a message from someone claiming to be me... it’s most likely not. If you don’t have my personal number and are unsure, just DM me on Instagram.

'If you receive anything suspicious, please send it to me directly so I can keep a record of it.

'Thank youuu (purple heart emoji, winking emoji),' she signed off.

Collins has worked in the media since joining IMG Media as an assistant five years ago.

Since 2022, the former waitress has served as a presenter for Premier League productions, which has led to opportunities to interview sports stars including Andy Robertson, John Terry, Bruno Fernandes, Conor Gallagher and Cody Gakpo.

Collins has also worked a number of events beyond the domestic league, such as Wimbledon and the 2025 Champions League final.

This year, she also covered the Open for Sky Sports from Royal Birkdale, and racing at York's Ebor Festival with ITV.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

In a recent development, so much for the fresh group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

Recent findings suggest that city will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

Industry observers note that they wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a newly introduced team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

Recent findings suggest that phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are upcoming to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

In a recent development, bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

Recent findings suggest that “In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca stated. “This indicates how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he revealed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

Industry observers note that city had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland said. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the significant stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

Recent findings suggest that for Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”.

In a recent development, 36 - Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.Inevitability. pic.twitter.com/HHbNadybxh.

“I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”.

“Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

“He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”.

In a recent development, enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

According to recent reports, manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that demonstrates a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

Recent findings suggest that porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

According to recent reports, “We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli remarked. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

Recent findings suggest that porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how his problems with alcohol left him contemplating suicide during his Manchester United career, as he opened up on the serious impact drinking had on his marriage to wife Coleen.

Rooney, 41, often came across as bullishly confident during his glittering playing career and then in the TV studio as a pundit, but says he is 'lucky' to have survived being thrown into the spotlight as a teenager - when he broke through at Everton at the age of 16.

The scrutiny cast upon him by the watching world led to Rooney hitting 'rock bottom' in his mid-twenties, whereby he recalls locking himself away in his house for two days to 'just drink'.

'This was at the best part of my career playing wise, I'd go home and sit in my games room and drink for two days,' he noted on Life At The Midpoint podcast. 'I'd get up for training, put some eyedrops in and chewing gum, and go to training.

Recent findings suggest that 'I couldn't deal with the pressures of everything and I made stupid choices when I was younger, off the pitch, and I really struggled to deal with it all to be honest. It was only when I spoke to Coleen and I spoke to my mum, and I opened up, it was only really when I vocally opened up that I needed help to get through it.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how he contemplated suicide during his 'lowest' moment.

He mentioned without the support of wife Coleen, he may not have 'survived' as he discussed how his life turned upside down after breaking through as a 16-year-old.

The Man United legend said he was binge-drinking for two days at the height of his career.

Recent findings suggest that 'When I look back now, you look back with regret because it's time lost. Kai was a baby at the time. I can look back and say I was selfish but I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with.

In a recent development, 'I got to a place where I was contemplating suicide. I didn't want to be around anyone, I didn't want to see anybody in the street, in the shops. I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else I struggled with.'.

Rooney added that his drinking problem caused strain on his marriage to childhood sweetheart Coleen, but he couldn't have survived without her help.

It has been revealed that 'Coleen helped me massively,' Rooney noted. 'I was speaking to a therapist to figure out what was up with me. Looking back, I was at the height of my career, just had a young son, just married, it should have been the happiest moment of my life but it was the lowest, because of the selfish acts I was taking.

Industry observers note that 'Coleen was massive. She could have walked away, it was that bad. She stuck by me and helped me get through it and obviously we had more kids.'.

Rooney also spoke candidly about his anxieties over his appearance.

The former Man United and England striker has overhauled his lifestyle, slimmed down, fixed his teeth and undergone a nose job, with fans amazed by his progress.

When asked about how he felt about the prospect of being exposed to a huge audience of viewers in the I'm A Celebrity jungle, Rooney admitted it was something he only now feels comfortable with after his glow-up.

'I wouldn't have been able to do it to be honest with you,' he told Gabby Logan on Life at the Midpoint podcast.

According to recent reports, 'They asked me last year to go in. I spoke to AngryGinge who I know and Aitch who I know and they were saying, "come in, imagine the three of us in there". It would have been chaos. I didn't think I'd physically be able to do it.

Wayne Rooney, pictured left on I'm a Celebrity and right in 2024, has admitted he used to feel self-conscious about his looks and weight.

Should footballers receive more support for mental health given pressure they face?

Sources indicate that 'I've always been self-conscious and always been conscious of my weight. I've always thought about how I look.

It has been revealed that 'Everything has fallen into place now where I know I feel better and know I look better than what I was. I looked at myself about a year ago and thought I did look probably about 50.

'And I was thinking, "you need to sort yourself out here" and so I was very self-conscious. I have been for my whole career for how I look or my weight, which at times I've struggled with.'.

Rooney had to endure a stomach-churning eating challenge on the launch show on I'm A Celebrity on Monday night, drinking fermented prawns and fish eyes and no doubt there's worse to come.

The slimmed-down Rooney was previously irked that some onlookers thought he had been taking weight loss injections rather than working hard to get in shape.

He previously explained to the Daily Mail: 'Apparently I've seen recently I've been taking this pen thing (weight loss jabs). It's a shame, because I'm working really hard to lose weight. Apparently I've been on the pen.'.

According to recent reports, he added on This Morning: 'I feel great, I haven't drank for a while. I just wanted to feel healthier and be healthier so I've changed my eating habits and training.

Sources indicate that 'Everyone's saying I'm on this pen thing. but I'm not, I've been working out to try and look better and be healthier.'.

Rooney has been praised for his physical turnaround and is favourite to win the show.

Rooney, pictured two years ago, cut down his drinking and changed his lifestyle.

Sources indicate that he also mentioned part of the motivation was to feel better for his time with the family. Rooney and his wife, who came second on I'm A Celebrity two years ago, are parents to Kai, 17, Klay, 13, Kit, ten, and Cass, eight.

Industry observers note that 'I've found more balance, it's helped me get back to a much better place. When I stopped playing, I got in a rut, I was drinking too much and not getting into the routine of training and I just thought, "You know what I want to enjoy the time with the kids whilst they're at this age, and with Coleen as well and I actually have been more present, more there for them,' he added.

At times during his playing days, Rooney was far from the model professional and back in 2012 admitted returning to Man United training seven pounds overweight.

In his book, My Decade in the Premier League, Rooney wrote of the summer of 2009: 'Early July: the first day back at pre-season training. I'm like most blokes, I put on a few pounds after a holiday. Even if I don't train for a week, I put on two or three, but when I get back to Carrington for the first day of work, I'm in for a shock. The scales in the club gym tell me I've put on a few more pounds than expected – seven. Seven!

'Then I remember – I drank a few bevvies while I was away. I'm stocky. I'm not like Ryan Giggs, all bone and lean muscle. But I gain weight quite easily. It's not a problem though.

'It's not as if the manager is leaning over my shoulder as the numbers come in, tutting and making jokes about me eating too many chip butties. Besides, I know I can shift it in a week or two. All the players are given loose training programmes to stick to while they're away, but they're optional.

'The club like us not to go overboard on the eating and drinking in the close-season break, so if I go abroad I like to get into the hotel gym three times a week to work on the treadmill and do some weight work.

'Coming back for pre-season after a few bevvies and a few weeks away from a ball is physically tough.'.

Despite Rooney's penchant for letting his hair down in the offseason, he was renowned for his work and commitment on the pitch and has recaptured that battling spirit to shed the weight in retirement.

Rooney, pictured during a match against Portugal at the 2006 World Cup in Germany, was not always fully committed to his diet during his glittering playing career.

The England legend has emerged as the betting favourite to be crowned King of the Jungle and is one of the highest-paid contestants in this year's show.

Bosses have reportedly offered Wayne more than his wife, who made a record-breaking £1.5million for her jungle stint.

Last week, Rooney remarked: 'This is probably the biggest exposure I've ever had, being on TV every night for three weeks.

'I hope people see I am a genuine person,' adding that he is a 'fun guy' who enjoys 'pranks'.

No doubt his dieting will be beneficial in having to deal with rations of long grain rice and beans in Australia for the duration of the show.

La Commissione esaminerà i dati al 30 settembre; a Formello si teme uno stop, ma resta la possibilità di intervenire sui conti.

La Lazio attende l’esame dei conti al 30 settembre per sapere come potrà operare nel mercato di gennaio: liberamente, a saldo zero o con un blocco. Secondo quanto riportato da Calciomercato.it, A Formello prevale un leggero pessimismo e il club si aspetta lo stop, che potrebbe però essere superato con le misure previste dall’articolo 90 delle Noif.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that la Commissione che ha sostituito la Covisoc valuterà la documentazione presentata dalla società. Se la Lazio avrà raggiunto il parametro dello 0,70%, potrà muoversi liberamente. Se la situazione sarà peggiorata rispetto a marzo, il mercato sarà bloccato; negli altri casi, il club opererà a saldo zero.

Sources indicate that la Lazio arriva da una sessione estiva a saldo zero. Al 31 marzo il rapporto tra costi e ricavi aveva superato la soglia dello 0,70%, raggiungendo lo 0,82%, con un disavanzo di circa 20 milioni di euro e un conseguente blocco parziale.

Industry observers note that nel recente bilancio, il costo del personale è salito da 98,2 a 104,6 milioni di euro e gli ammortamenti dei calciatori da 32,7 a 38,4 milioni. Il monte ingaggi è invece sceso da 79,5 a circa 75 milioni. Il club ha inoltre inserito a bilancio 7 milioni legati a Polymarket, limitati alla quota del primo anno dell’accordo quinquennale di sponsorizzazione, bloccato dall’autorità.

Incideranno anche gli incassi del botteghino e i mancati introiti europei. La scorsa stagione la Lazio aveva messo a bilancio circa 20 milioni dagli ingressi allo stadio; in quella attuale, lo sciopero del tifo ha bloccato questa entrata. In caso di stop al mercato, la società potrebbe pagare una sanzione e coprire l’eventuale deficit per rientrare nei parametri. Lotito sta cercando di sistemare il passivo inserendo crediti o dilazionando alcuni pagamenti, in particolare quelli relativi al periodo Covid.

The French media have come down hard on a number of Premier League players in the national team after less than impressive displays under upcoming coach Zinedine Zidane.

Over the break France scraped a 2-1 win against Turkey in the Nations League but only after an unexpected 3-1 loss to Italy at the San Siro.

And among the team's most glaring underperformers – according to some observers in France – were Chelsea's Malo Gusto, Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert and Liverpool's £123million summer signing Bradley Barcola.

French outlet RMC Sport was particularly critical of the pair, with journalist Alexandre Jaquin describing Gusto as 'probably the one who disappointed the most during this second international window of the Zidane era'.

Jaquin added: 'Fielded in Italy despite little playing time with Chelsea, the right-back completely fell into the San Siro furnace.

Malo Gusto struggled has been under fire from the French media after a string of poor performances under Zinedine Zidane.

The honeymoon period is over for Zidane, according to French media.

Recent findings suggest that 'Overwhelmed by his opponents' energy and little helped by Michael Olise's lack of defensive defense, the former Lyon player lived a nightmare in Lombardy, notably conceding a penalty. A match rapidly erased from his memory.'.

RMC was not much kinder to Barcola as well, concluding: 'The Liverpool winger was one of the few to start both matches in November. But in the end, it didn't really take off, neither in Italy nor against Turkey.

Recent findings suggest that 'Sometimes on his left flank, sometimes in a false nine, the former PSG supersub was often imprecise in his final moves. Like his failed one-on-one against the Turks, the Lyon native lacked accuracy and composure to make the opposing goal tremble.'.

It has been revealed that even newcomer Adrien Truffert was not afforded some sympathy as Jaquin said: 'After a rather satisfying debut in October, the Bournemouth left-back benefited from the trust of Zinedine Zidane, who played him in Italy. But despite his efforts, the Cherries player delivered a very mixed performance.'.

This recent criticism adds to growing dissatisfaction in France with the overall state of the national team under Zidane.

Liverpool's £123million man is yet to make a major impact for club or country so far this season.

According to recent reports, journalist Walid Acherchour made his feelings known on the After Foot programme, saying: 'Zidane hit a wall of reality with this second international break... I found the attitude of some individuals against Turkey to be very poor.

It has been revealed that 'In the second half against Italy and in the match against Turkey, how do you manage without the ball when you're being torn apart in midfield? Zidane will have to work on all these questions.'.

Acherchour closed by saying bluntly: 'The honeymoon is over.'.

After an ultimately disappointing World Cup in which the French were again by Spain in a major semi-final – following their Euro 2024 exit – long-term manager Didier Deschamps left after 14 years in charge.

Legendary midfielder Zidane succeeded him in the summer and has already led France to the top of their Nations League group – but some of his players may have to go much further to win over their critics.

Dal ritiro con il Vejle all’offerta biancoceleste: il dirigente ripercorre il lavoro svolto con il difensore danese.

It has been revealed that mario Nicolae ripercorre il percorso di Oliver Provstgaard, dal Vejle alla Lazio, e ritiene che il difensore potrebbe fare bene anche all’Inter, club al quale viene accostato. Secondo quanto riportato da TuttoMercatoWeb, Il dirigente, che oggi lavora al Rapid Bucarest, racconta la fiducia data al danese quando era un giovane dell’accademia e le tappe che lo hanno portato al trasferimento in biancoceleste.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Nicolae aveva già definito Provstgaard «un vero gioiello pronto al grande salto». Ora ricorda il progetto costruito attorno a lui, l’offerta della Lazio e il ruolo avuto dai suoi agenti nell’operazione.

In a recent development, nicolae incontrò Provstgaard al Vejle, in Danimarca. Il dirigente ripercorre i suoi primi mesi nel club e la preparazione del ritiro: «Quando sono arrivato la squadra era ultima in classifica in Danimarca, a dicembre. Ci stavamo organizzando per il ritiro ad Antalya in Turchia, stavamo facendo la rosa di chi sarebbe venuto con noi. Ero nuovo, ho sentito tante opinioni tra proprietà e staff sui giocatori interessanti, quelli con cui proseguire. Mi hanno accennato di Oliver che in quel momento era giovane, veniva dall'accademia ma arrivava dai problemi ai crociati e non giocava da mesi».

Nonostante l’infortunio e i mesi senza giocare, le qualità del difensore convinsero Nicolae a portarlo in Turchia: «Però era giovane, di prospettiva, fisicamente molto interessante e intelligente. Mi è sembrato giusto portarlo subito in ritiro con noi. Ho iniziato a conoscerlo e ho rinnovato subito il suo contratto!».

Recent findings suggest that la scelta di coinvolgerlo nel ritiro fu dunque il primo passo di un percorso che, secondo Nicolae, richiedeva fiducia e lavoro condiviso. Il dirigente aveva ascoltato le valutazioni interne prima di puntare sul giovane centrale.

Industry observers note that il successivo cambio di allenatore diede continuità al progetto sul difensore. Nicolae racconta: «A marzo abbiamo cambiato allenatore, abbiamo preso un tecnico croato molto giovane come Ivan Prelec, che aveva esperienza nell'accademia della Dinamo Zagabria e quindi coi ragazzi. Gli ho accennato il progetto Provstgaard, lì siamo retrocessi ma Oliver ha esordito tra i pro in Serie A. Il secondo anno siamo tornati subito su, vincendo la Serie B danese con lui titolarissimo».

It has been revealed that nicolae sottolinea che non si trattò soltanto di credere nelle qualità del giocatore. «Non ho solo avuto fiducia e visione su Provstgaard ma c'è stato anche un progetto con lui, con allenatore e proprietà, abbiamo detto che era un prospetto della società con cui c'era da lavorare per creare un prodotto per una grande lega europea. Gli abbiamo dato fiducia anche quando, e capitava poche volte, non giocava bene», spiega.

Al lavoro del club si aggiunse quello di Oliver. Nicolae ne ripercorre i progressi, dall’Under 21 e dalla fascia di capitano della selezione giovanile fino al posto da titolare nella massima serie danese. Ricorda anche la cessione, avvenuta nella settimana in cui il Vejle fu venduto, e la propria successiva partenza: «Ha lavorato come un pazzo: è arrivato in Under 21, poi è stato capitano dell'Under, in Serie A poi ha giocato chiaramente da titolare. Poi siamo riusciti a venderlo alla Lazio proprio nella settimana in cui il club è stato poi venduto e poi sono andato via anche io… La Lazio ha fatto la miglior offerta, c'era il Pisa con un'offerta ufficiale e anche altri club. Tramite i suoi agenti, che avevano già Isaksen alla Lazio, è stata un'operazione importante e chiaramente questo è stato un fattore». La Lazio presentò l’offerta migliore; il Pisa ne aveva formulata una ufficiale e c’erano anche altre società interessate.

According to recent reports, nel percorso al Vejle fu importante anche Raul Albentosa, capitano spagnolo della squadra. Nicolae collega l’ambizione di Provstgaard al sostegno ricevuto dal compagno: «Ha sempre voluto crescere, ha sempre voluto arrivare in un top club nel Mondo. Al Vejle abbiamo fatto grandi cose insieme, è stata l'esperienza perfetta per lui. E' cresciuto al fianco del nostro capitano spagnolo, Raul Albentosa, che è stato un fratello per lui. Oltre 100 presenze in Liga e lo ha guidato passo dopo passo in questo progetto di due anni e mezzo».

In a recent development, per Nicolae, Midtjylland e Copenhagen avrebbero rappresentato un salto importante ma interno al calcio danese. Riteneva invece Provstgaard pronto per una grande squadra anche fuori dalla Danimarca: «Era già pronto per andare in un top club. Poteva andare al Midtjylland, al Copenhagen, ma sarebbe stato solo un salto di livello interno anche se molto importante. Dal Vejle alla Lazio è stato il grande salto, chiaramente, ma sì, era già pronto. L'Italia ha sempre apprezzato i giocatori scandinavi, non è un caso che ci abbiano pensato. Per me vederlo in prima pagina su un grande quotidiano è un grande orgoglio».

Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under newly introduced head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.
  • It has been revealed that on the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness.
  • And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under newly introduced head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

It has been revealed that on the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face noted it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Sources indicate that mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

Industry observers note that there are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ newly introduced head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A significant European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

It has been revealed that “I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Sources indicate that liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

According to recent reports, as does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

Recent findings suggest that there was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

In a recent development, llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

Industry observers note that this is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

It has been revealed that atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

Recent findings suggest that “I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”.

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE.

Sources indicate that andoni Iraola has been speaking to TNT Sports and has confirmed that it was just cramp for the likes of Bradley Barcola, rather than an injury. Milos Kerkez also went off late with what appears to be just cramp.

Atletico had more possession in the second half but Liverpool were much the better side after the break.

"We can achieve everything we want." 💪Dominik Szoboszlai full of belief after Liverpool's Champions League victory over Atletico Madrid 👀🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ebSvagW4yx.

In a recent development, there is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ.

First Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b.

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Just 60 seconds remain at Anfield.

There will be five added minutes.

Sources indicate that liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Recent findings suggest that kerkez is at the moment down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

It has been revealed that liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,.

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

In a recent development, alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a latest contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The big challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The newly introduced Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on.

He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

Sources indicate that “I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”.
