Industry observers note that liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

According to recent reports, andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

Industry observers note that “It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”.

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”.

Declan Rice has agreed a new five-year deal at Arsenal that will run until the summer of 2031 - with goalkeeper David Raya set to join him in committing his future to the club.

The England midfielder is expected to sign the new contract soon, which is set to put him alongside Bukayo Saka as Arsenal's top earner. Saka is on a deal worth over £350,000 a week.

It has been revealed that and Raya, 31, is understood to have agreed a deal in principle to extend his terms. Both players' existing deals expire in 2028.

Rice joined Arsenal in 2023 for £105million from West Ham and has established himself as the fulcrum of their midfield, helping steer them to the Premier League title last season.

The 27-year-old played 55 games in all competitions last season as the Gunners reached their first Champions League final since 2006, but lost out to Paris Saint-Germain.

His contract talks have been ongoing from at least March and are now finalised.

Raya joined Arsenal from Brentford on loan in the same summer, and signed a permanent deal a year later.

Declan Rice has agreed a new-five year deal at Arsenal that will run until the summer of 2031.

David Raya has agreed a deal in principle to stay on, with his current deal expiring in 2028.

Rice had confirmed a latest deal was close over the weekend when speaking on international duty with England.

'I've been extremely lucky that I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career.

'I've always been stable in the clubs I've been at.

'A latest contract is hopefully on the horizon soon.

'I'm extremely lucky that I'm at a club like Arsenal, where my manager [Mikel Arteta] and my team-mates put so much energy in me.

'I'm extremely lucky I don't have to think about that stuff.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A highly anticipated Bundesliga match between upstart clubs Elversberg and Freiburg has ended with Julian Schuster’s Breisgauer picking up all three points via a narrow 0-1 away victory over Vincent Wagner’s Elversberg.
  • It has been revealed that wagner made two changes to the team that lined up against Borussia Dortmund just prior to the international break.
  • Neither team could be accused of being complacent in the opening ten minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A highly anticipated Bundesliga match between upstart clubs Elversberg and Freiburg has ended with Julian Schuster’s Breisgauer picking up all three points via a narrow 0-1 away victory over Vincent Wagner’s Elversberg. Freiburg – along with Niko Kovac’s Borussia Dortmund – have both taken advantage of record champions Bayern Munich dropping points against Cologne last night. Freiburg draw level with Bayern on points while Dortmund top the table after also narrowly edging out Borussia Mönchengladbach 0-1 away.

It has been revealed that wagner made two changes to the team that lined up against Borussia Dortmund just prior to the international break. Jan Gyamerah started at right back over Luca Sirch while Cole Campbell took the place of Germany U21 international Maurice Krattenmacher on the left wing. Schuster, meanwhile, employed just one change to the XI that began against Union Berlin 13 days ago. The star of that victory, Yuito Suzuki, was given a break after returning from international duty with Japan. German veteran Lucas Höler started in place of Suzuki in the No. 10 slot.

Neither team could be accused of being complacent in the opening ten minutes. In point of fact, willingness to intensely engage in direct duels remained high on both sides. Amid the many changes in possession, however, neither team was able to achieve much of a breakthrough. Freiburg did win a pair of corners and Igor Matanovic came close to earning a chance in the 9th minute. It would nevertheless be unfair to say that the Breisgauer guests looked the better squad. Possession remained split down the middle throughout the first quarter-of-an-hour.

Recent findings suggest that elversberg won their first corner in the 18th minute thanks to some hard work on the dribble from Leverkusen loanee Francis Onyeka. The hosts were able to swing the ball into the box several times after the set-piece, yet couldn’t produce an effort on target. Maximilian Rohr and Lukasz Poreba managed to dig out another Elversberg corner in the 23rd minute. David Mokwa forced a stellar save from Mio Backhaus off the corner, but the Saarland hosts again failed to get the ball headed goal-ward on the successive dead-ball.

After the half-hour mark passed, the SVE began to look a tad more lively and creative. Gyamerah, Lukas Petkov, and Felix Keidel repeatedly got some solid attack charges going up the SVE right. The fact that the hosts gained an upper hand optically still produced little. Mokwa saw his attempt at a spectacular bicycle kick blocked in the 34th. Onyeka spurned a lovely play-in from Gyamerah in the 40th by losing the ball in the box. Apart from drawing a frustration-fueled yellow card out of Freiburg’s Jan-Niklas Beste, the promoted club had nothing to show for their efforts.

The match unquestionably maintained its intensity while undeniably featuring a steady loss of tempo.

Sources indicate that neither head coach opted to employ changes at the half. To the candid observer, these decisions were quite apparent. Schuster’s guests added a slight element of risk to their game, yet were still constrained by the fact that “paint the corner” passing around the box didn’t facilitate any danger. At the other end, Elversberg were gifted counter opportunities on both flanks in the opening ten minutes after the start, but noticeably lacked the pace to take true advantage of the accorded space. Onyeka came closest to creating a chance at the hour-mark, finding himself stymied centrally by a Maximilian Eggestein block.

According to recent reports, the hosts eventually found themselves punished for failing to turn a slight optical advantage into a lead. Beste latched onto a long launch from SCF defender Philipp Lienhart in the 68th minute. After shielding the ball skillfully against SVE challenger Rohr, Beste actually inadvertently set up Igor Matanovic with a layoff. The Croat marksman nevertheless didn’t hesitate, reacting sharply to smack the ball deftly into the bottom right corner. Matanovic’s impressive ninth goal across all competitions this season gave the visiting Schwarzwälder a 1-0 lead.

Recent findings suggest that with the deadlock finally broken, the encounter rapidly became more entertaining. A Keidel-led counter-attack shortly after the opening goal nearly led to an equalizer, but SVE captain Lukas Pinckert ultimately shot wide. Not long after being subbed on, Suzuki thought he had doubled Freiburg’s advantage in the 76th minute. The goal was chalked off due to a narrow offside decision.

Plenty of action ensued for a time until Schuster’s men settled into a more compact block and the Freiburg coach sent on some attacking reinforcements. As the clock ticked on towards full-time, Freiburg looked the more likely team to score. Fresh SCF attackers Vincenzo Grifo and Keisuke Goto opened up more space in the SCF attacking third. Eggestein and Philipp Treu saw late tries for the 2-0 blocked.

Gary Neville launches surprise defence of Diogo Dalot and names the THREE defenders Mauricio Pochettino should sell before Man United boo boy

  • Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.
  • The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026.

Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.

The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.

But as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford, Neville urged the new manager not to immediately expel the defender, despite his drop-off in form.

'I think if he was in a decent back four he'd be alright,' Neville told Stick to United co-host Mark Goldbridge on Tuesday. 'But he's got a shocking back four alongside him.

'Positionally he's not great. He could be better on the ball. He could be better at everything he does. Of course he could. I just think he's such an easy target, Dalot. I honestly do.'.

Neville admitted that sometimes he listens to his fellow Man United-supporting friends deriding Dalot and wonders 'are they watching something that I don't see?'.

Gary Neville has defended Man United star Diogo Dalot - arguing that he has team-mates who are far weaker.

The Portugal international has come in for heavy criticism from supporters this season.

But in his opinion, there are three defenders that he would let go in the 'first wave' of changes in Manchester.

Recent findings suggest that 'I'd be getting (Noussair) Mazraoui well gone before him,' he continued. 'I'd be getting (Lisandro) Martinez gone well before him. I'll be getting (Matthijs) De Ligt gone well before him.

Recent findings suggest that '(De Ligt has) got one substantial problem. He doesn’t play football. If a player is injury prone and doesn't play football, just because he hasn't played doesn't mean to say that he should go above a player who's played every single week and he's throwing his hand up. You want someone who's actually reliable and play. De Ligt has to go. De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui.'.

Another stalwart in the team that Neville was keen to have a second chance under Pochettino was Luke Shaw.

It has been revealed that 'He will keep Shaw because he knows him and he'll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries,' he added. 'So he'll have to manage him. So he'll have to bring a left back in. But let's just say who he'll keep.

Industry observers note that 'He'll keep Shaw. He'll keep (Harry) Maguire because he'll trust him and he'll think that he's basically a soldier and someone who can do a job for him.

'He'll keep (Leny) Yoro because I think he'll think "I've got something there that I can work with". (But) I think he's a little bit gangly, all over the place right now. And he looks like he's going to slip every time. He's got that sort of Bambi-on-ice (look).

'Physically what will happen is with Yoro, he'll go one way or the other. I like the fact he's been brought into the French team. It tells me sometimes you just have got to connect the dots and think, "okay, well, if they think he's good, then we must be missing something here because we're not seeing it yet, are we?".'.

Neville went on to suggest that Yoro was lacking the connection within his body that Premier League rivals such as Jeremy Jacquet are already able to harness – something Sir Alex Ferguson had identified in Rio Ferdinand when he was at West Ham.

Like Ferdinand, Neville backed Yoro to flourish as he taps into that connection and improves his strength and stability.

It has been revealed that 'So Yoro he will keep: Yoro, Maguire and Shaw I think he'll keep and I think he'll keep Dalot. To start with,' Neville said. 'He'll have to bring in three defenders to go above them. Let's be clear. He'll have to bring in three defenders.

Industry observers note that 'Mazraoui I would lose, De Ligt I would lose because he's injury prone. Martinez 100 per cent. 100 per cent. 100 per cent.'.

As well as struggling for form this season, Martinez has been a challenging presence in the Man United squad this term, boldly calling out the Man United hierarchy during a firebrand interview last month.

Neville was more interested in latest head coach Mauricio Pochettino despatching Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt.

Lisandro Martinez has been an unsettled presence in the side this season and hit out at the club's recruiting last month.

The Argentina star implied that he was disappointed with the club's recruitment strategy over the summer, and was forced to hold clear-the-air talks to smooth his return to the side.

Neville added that he would send Ayden Heaven on loan to get experience in the lower divisions to 'build' his ability up, as it was borderline 'unfair' to be 'putting him in' the side at present.

But not all of the changes can come promptly for Pochettino, who has little time before taking charge of Man United against Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.

'First wave, end of the season,' Neville clarified of what he believes Pochettino's blueprint for change will be. 'No, he can't get rid of (them all) in January.

'He has to bring one or two defenders in January if he can. But he can't get rid of all those in his first wave. He's only got one month till January.'.

The drawn-out process of sacking Carrick began last week when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada flew to Monaco for talks with co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer ownership group.

While his future was on the chopping block, Carrick held training sessions at Carrington before the axe finally swung last Thursday.

Pochettino was appointed days later and gave a tearful farewell press conference ahead of his penultimate game with the United States national team on Saturday.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he told the press. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

Sources indicate that ‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

According to recent reports, ‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

Recent findings suggest that the 23-year-old believes that his understanding with Beste, rather than simple good fortune, made the decisive difference. Recent findings suggest that the striker also recalled his earlier observations about the special chemistry within Schuster’s squad. That collective understanding has helped Freiburg negotiate difficult Bundesliga encounters, including Saturday’s hard-fought victory over a spirited Elversberg side.

The latest success follows Freiburg’s 2-0 home victory against Union Berlin before the international break and further strengthens the Breisgau club’s position near the top of the Bundesliga table.

The south Baden side responded to a 1-3 home defeat against Bayern on matchday seven by defeating Wolfsburg in the Pokal. They’ve not lost since, capturing five consecutive victories on the spin.

Sources indicate that “I know that Niki likes making that run,” Matanovic told Get German Football News in the mixed zone. “And the way he laid the ball off, I think a lot of people will say it was accidental. I think he wanted it exactly that way. I’m convinced of that.”.

It has been revealed that “I already told you at the beginning of the season that this team is really special,” the striker continued. “I had the feeling that we had an instinctive understanding. Actually, it’s not just a feeling. We really do have that understanding.”.

“Everyone knows which runs the other players make, and Niki knows that I’ll naturally follow his run,” Matanovic explained. “He laid the ball off perfectly for me, allowing me to put it away nicely.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that freiburg striker Igor Matanovic believes his team’s newfound ability to grind out difficult victories represents a significant step forward under head coach Julian Schuster. Speaking to Get German Football News in the mixed zone after Saturday’s 1-0 Bundesliga victory over Elversberg, the Croatian international explained why Freiburg are now consistently collecting points in matches that might previously have ended in frustrating draws.

Matanovic’s 68th-minute winner against the promoted Saarland club extended Freiburg’s winning streak to five matches across all competitions. The Breisgauer have recovered impressively from their October struggles, defeating Wolfsburg in the DFB-Pokal before adding victories against Augsburg, Trabzonspor, Union Berlin, and Elversberg.

The latest success also moved Freiburg level on points with Bayern Munich near the top of the Bundesliga table.

According to recent reports, the 23-year-old believes Freiburg’s improvement reflects considerably more than a fortunate run of results. Matanovic emphasized the squad’s collective resilience, suggesting that the team’s current momentum has been built upon a healthy foundation and a willingness to discuss shortcomings openly.

The striker specifically recalled Freiburg’s response to three consecutive defeats earlier in the campaign, praising his teammates for refusing to allow the setbacks to undermine their confidence.

Saturday’s hard-fought victory provided another illustration of that mentality. As documented in GGFN‘s match report and player ratings, Freiburg struggled to create clear opportunities against a spirited Elversberg side before finally breaking through in the second half.

Matanovic explained that maintaining concentration and relying on familiar tactical principles were particularly key in such circumstances. Aggressive pressing, collective defensive work, and persistence in winning possession eventually helped Freiburg create the decisive opening.

In a recent development, “It’s tremendous. Obviously, it’s very nice to be collecting the points as well,” Matanovic said when asked about Freiburg’s five consecutive victories. “I think that’s the difference compared to last season. What we were missing were the points. We often played well, but then we’d come away with just one point. Now we’re winning the dirty games.”.

“Even recently against Union Berlin, you know how unpleasant they can be to play against, and we still managed to win 2-0,” the Croatian continued. “There’s genuinely a very high level of quality in this team, and of course we’re enjoying a certain flow. But the flow we have comes from this healthy foundation that we can always rely upon. I often mention the three consecutive defeats we suffered. How many teams collapse after something like that? How many lose their confidence?”.

“But we always get back to basics,” Matanovic went on. “We address things openly and honestly, and that’s how we find our way back into our flow. Right now, we’re simply very, very difficult opponents to face. You have to maintain your focus, especially when you’re not creating many chances or opportunities. Then you have these basics you can rely upon. Keep pushing forward, press high, make life difficult for the opposition, and block plenty of balls.”.

Sources indicate that “I think we also won possession back many times in the first half,” Matanovic concluded. “That’s something we force through our own efforts, and that’s how we eventually create scoring chances again. There weren’t many chances, but I think we could even have rewarded ourselves with more goals in the end.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the newly introduced Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4.

It has been revealed that in five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

Recent findings suggest that “That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” noted Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”.

Industry observers note that in the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Sources indicate that their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

Sources indicate that “With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” stated Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”.

There was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

To lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r.

In a recent development, A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

Industry observers note that even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Sources indicate that throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

It has been revealed that despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

It has been revealed that in keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm.

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN.

"We missed so many massive chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH.

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Wed, October 21: Bayern Munich (A) 8pm.

Wed, November 4: Slavia Prague (A) 8pm.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm.

Wed, December 9: Real Madrid (H) 8pm.

Wed, January 20: Real Betis (A) 8pm.

Recent findings suggest that “Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” mentioned Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”.

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”.

It has been revealed that couple that with his impressive chemistry with fresh arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

The action has concluded around Europe tonight so here are your final scores from this week’s second night of European football:.

Possession: Napoli 42%-58% Arsenal.

Touches in opposition box: 9-52.

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

Recent findings suggest that they kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Here is the goal that won it for them, courtesy of their captain:.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4.

Napoli are fighting, but Arsenal hold fast.

Milinković-Savić waves his players downfield for the final minute but Olivera can’t control the ball well.

Four minutes will be added on here as Napoli are being urged on by their fans.

Industry observers note that arsenal need to hold onto the ball and manage the game intelligently here. Zubimendi goes in for a challenge though and hauls down his man, and Napoli get the ball back. Odegaard goes into the book for his protests.

Napoli again, still trying to get their goal and De Bruyne gives them a chance with a through ball to David Neres, but the striker can’t get on the ball.

Arsenal are almost caught as the ball falls to De Bruyne on the left of the box, with a clear look at Raya in goal, but the Belgian crosses the ball thinking he’s got a team-mate there to put it away but there is no one and it is a huge let-off for Arsenal.

After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a newly introduced attempt to claim their white whale.

Their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under new manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they at the moment sit 12th in the league.

They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha has refused to rule out repeating his controversial crown celebration despite previous assurances from Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp that the gesture would no longer be performed. Speaking after scoring the winning goal in Saturday’s 1-0 Bundesliga victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach, the 26-year-old defended his religious convictions while suggesting that the controversy surrounding his celebrations had been exaggerated.

Sources indicate that nmecha’s 80th-minute winner secured three crucial points for Niko Kovac’s side, sending Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table. The in-form German international has now scored five league goals this season, including three in his last two appearances. Nmecha’s most recent goal celebration till exhibited religious overtones, though the Dortmund professional did not repeat the crowning gesture that sparked the controversy in the first place. Nmecha spoke on the matter afterwards.

In a recent development, the controversy began following Dortmund’s 2-1 victory over SV Elversberg before the international break. Nmecha celebrated both goals by symbolically removing a crown and placing it on the ground. The gesture is associated with the evangelical football network Ballers in God, whose activities and reported positions on homosexuality and other social issues have attracted criticism.

Get German Football News previously reported on Dortmund’s response to the controversy, including objections raised by the club’s Fan and Supporters Department. Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke subsequently appealed to Nmecha to reconsider the gesture, emphasizing the importance of avoiding unnecessary divisions among supporters.

It has been revealed that germany head coach Jürgen Klopp later indicated that the matter had been resolved following a personal conversation with Nmecha. Klopp explained that the midfielder had agreed not to repeat the celebration in its controversial form. Nmecha indeed opted for a different celebration after scoring against Gladbach, sliding towards the corner flag before kneeling and crossing his arms over his chest. After the full-time whistle, Nmecha dropped to his knees and engaged in prayer.

According to recent reports, dortmund sporting director Ole Book defended Nmecha’s right to express his Christian faith, distinguishing Saturday’s celebration from the gesture that had provoked criticism. Meanwhile, Ballers in God subsequently shared images of Nmecha’s latest celebration on social media, interpreting three of his gestures as symbolizing a direct communication of the player’s Christian faith.

“What people were saying didn’t ring true to me,” Nmecha told Sky Germany. “That celebration was simply about my faith, laying the crown on the ground for Jesus and giving him the glory. That doesn’t mean I’ll never do that celebration again.”.

Dortmund sporting director Ole Book also addressed Nmecha’s celebrations after the final whistle, defending the midfielder’s right to express his Christian faith. Book considered it legitimate for Nmecha to demonstrate his desire to thank Jesus and God for his goal, while emphasizing that the midfielder had refrained from repeating the controversial gesture.

“He didn’t perform the controversial part of the celebration today,” Book explained.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that the extraordinary scenes began before kickoff when the Bundesliga club announced that its stadium-wide sound system had suffered a technical failure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eintracht Frankfurt supporters provided one of the most heartwarming moments of Saturday’s Bundesliga action after a technical malfunction silenced the sound system at Deutsche Bank Park. Rather than allow the disruption to spoil the occasion, the Frankfurt faithful took matters into their own hands, providing their own musical accompaniment ahead of the Eagles’ 1-0 home victory over TSG Hoffenheim.

It has been revealed that the extraordinary scenes began before kickoff when the Bundesliga club announced that its stadium-wide sound system had suffered a technical failure. A message displayed on the stadium’s video screens warned supporters that the usual announcements and musical accompaniment would be unavailable until further notice. An unusually quiet atmosphere accompanied the players’ warm-ups. Frankfurt’s famously passionate supporters nevertheless had other ideas.

At the request of the stadium announcer, who could still be heard faintly, supporters in Frankfurt’s Nordwestkurve began singing the club’s traditional anthem, Im Herzen von Europa, without any musical accompaniment. The spontaneous performance proved particularly fitting given the song’s history. The beloved Eintracht anthem was originally recorded by Frankfurt’s police choir, whose rendition has become an integral part of the club’s home matchday tradition.

On Saturday, however, the supporters themselves assumed responsibility for the performance.

The club couldn’t resist making light of the unusual circumstances.

According to recent reports, “‘Im Herzen von Europa’, today performed not by the police choir, but by the stadium choir. That’s a first,” Eintracht observed in its matchday coverage. Nor did the impromptu entertainment stop with the anthem. Supporters also enthusiastically took over the team announcements, shouting out the starting lineup and providing a suitably rousing welcome as both teams emerged onto the pitch.

The technical difficulties had threatened to deprive the afternoon of its familiar atmosphere. Instead, they had given the Frankfurt faithful an opportunity to demonstrate precisely why the Waldstadion remains one of German football’s most atmospheric venues.

Industry observers note that the singing continued into the opening stages of the match, with the Nordwestkurve providing vocal encouragement as Adi Hütter’s side sought to make the most of their home advantage. Frankfurt’s supporters were rewarded in the 25th minute when Jonathan Burkardt finished an excellent attacking move to give the hosts the lead.

Recent findings suggest that although faint goal music and an announcement could reportedly be heard amid the technical difficulties, the home fans hardly needed any encouragement to celebrate. There was further excitement before halftime when goalkeeper Noah Atubolu saved Andrej Kramaric’s penalty in the 41st minute. Frankfurt then received a spot kick of their own, only for Hoffenheim goalkeeper Oliver Baumann to deny Burkardt three minutes later.

In a recent development, the stadium’s sound system was finally restored for the second half, but the supporters had already ensured that the unusual afternoon would be remembered for something considerably more enjoyable than a technical malfunction. Frankfurt ultimately protected their narrow lead to claim all three points, securing a third consecutive Bundesliga home victory.

Eintracht CEO Axel Hellmann was rather less enthusiastic about the technical difficulties. Speaking after the match, the club executive used the incident to renew his calls for a new stadium, pointing to increasingly frequent problems with the ageing arena’s electricity, lighting, and other infrastructure. Hellmann maintained that the situation would only deteriorate in the coming years and reiterated the need for a replacement venue, ideally completed by 2038.

Recent findings suggest that one can certainly appreciate Hellmann’s concerns. Nevertheless, there is a certain irony in the fact that the stadium’s shortcomings should become so apparent on an afternoon when its supporters demonstrated precisely what makes the place so special.

As Get German Football News noted in a feature on Germany’s most beloved traditional stadiums last November, the Waldstadion occupies a particularly cherished place in the hearts of the German footballing public. Nestled in the forest south of Frankfurt’s bustling financial district, the historic ground retains an identity that no corporate naming-rights agreement has ever managed to displace.

Whatever the future holds for the Waldstadion, Saturday’s events offered another reminder that the most important component of Frankfurt’s famous home atmosphere requires neither electricity nor expensive technology.

Just a few thousand willing voices.

#61476. The curious case of Sebastien Pocognoli looks certain to have a grisly ending... the SFA have hired a dud

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1410 w)
📖 Baca

The curious case of Sebastien Pocognoli looks certain to have a grisly ending... the SFA have hired a dud

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1410 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 14:13 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:26 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Of all the many stories written by F Scott Fitzgerald, one of the finest authors and wordsmiths of his time, The Great Gatsby will forever remain his masterpiece.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:13 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:26 EST, 17 November 2026.

Of all the many stories written by F Scott Fitzgerald, one of the finest authors and wordsmiths of his time, The Great Gatsby will forever remain his masterpiece.

In some of his other work written as he travelled across Europe, Fitzgerald also had a line about Switzerland, describing it as a ‘country where very few things begin, but many things end.’.

It is a curious quote and, like much of Fitzgerald’s work, is open to interpretation. As the man who also wrote The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, curiosity was a common theme.

As for the Curious Case of Sebastien Pocognoli, Switzerland may, indeed, be the country where everything came to an end.

What unfolded in St Gallen on Monday evening was a horror show. Scotland were battered 4-0 by Switzerland’s B team. There is no way to sugar-coat a result like that, no way to dress it up as anything other than an embarrassment. They played OK for half an hour and then fell apart.

Pocognoli claimed afterwards that there were positives to be taken and how some of Scotland’s football was the best they have produced across his six matches in charge.

Sebastien Pocognoli is facing serious questions after a miserable Nations League campaign.

Utter nonsense. That was a manager clutching at straws at the end of a Nations League campaign which has been an unmitigated disaster pretty much from start to finish.

Let’s go back to the very start here. After Steve Clarke had pushed the Scottish Football Association (SFA) into awarding him a fresh four-year contract, only to then walk away after the World Cup, it was a chance for a fresh start.

On the day when Pocognoli was unveiled as the upcoming head coach in August, Ian Maxwell and Craig Mulholland, the SFA’s chief executive and chief football officer, were beaming with positivity.

They told us all how data and AI had been used in the recruitment process, and how several clubs across Europe had been chasing Pocognoli.

They clearly viewed it as a coup to have landed the 39-year-old Belgian, who had won a league title in his homeland with Union Saint-Gilloise before a short stint with Monaco.

Recent findings suggest that what would the data say now? Six games played, two wins, a draw and three defeats, five goals scored and ten conceded, seven points and a lousy third-placed finish in Group B1.

In a recent development, both of those wins came against a North Macedonian side who lost all six of their games. They were a pub team – and Scotland still struggled to beat them at Hampden last Friday night.

Pocognoli was unable to inspire any resistance as his side succumbed to defeat in St Gallen.

According to recent reports, scotland lost 7-0 on aggregate to Switzerland over the two games. Against Slovenia, a 0-0 draw on the opening day in Ljubljana was then followed with a woeful 2-1 defeat at Hampden.

According to recent reports, all of which begs a very simple question. Where, exactly, are the grounds for optimism here? How is this getting any better?

When Pocognoli arrived, he spoke about trying to change the style of play, get Scotland playing a more exciting brand of football, whilst bringing through a new generation of players.

In a recent development, it was not a rebuild. He inherited a group of players who were accustomed to success under Clarke and who qualified for three tournaments out of a possible four.

His remit was to help Scotland take the next step in major tournaments. With a more dynamic style of play, the job was to help the nation take the next step.

Sources indicate that there has been no revolution thus far. No evidence whatsoever that this coach is capable of delivering results nor a better style of play.

It has been revealed that there is no satisfaction to be taken in any of this. When Pocognoli was appointed, it was, in the eyes of this observer, an interesting and progressive move.

SFA chiefs Craig Mulholland and Ian Maxwell proudly unveil new boss Pocognoli at Hampden.

Over the past 48 hours or so, there has been a lot of revisionism from some folk about Clarke. ‘Aye, the grass isn’t always greener...’.

According to recent reports, that’s garbage. Clarke’s time was up with Scotland. He should never have been handed a latest four-year deal in the first place. At least he did the right thing in resigning after the World Cup.

It has been revealed that the whole thing was finished. The problem is that the SFA look like they have appointed a total dud as his successor. Both of those things can be true at the same time.

According to recent reports, it is also worth remembering that the only reason we arrived at Pocognoli is because Clarke walked away. The SFA did not instigate any change.

The hiring of a newly introduced head coach was not a proactive change of direction, but a reactive move from an executive body who became accepting of Clarke’s limitations and allowed him to position them over a barrel.

Listen, there is nothing inherently wrong with using data and metrics in football. It’s the modern way. Using data to inform decisions and recruitment processes is smart business.

But the data in itself is no guarantee of success. There are some intangibles in football, things which are harder to quantify. Like a manager who blindly sticks to a system which is patently ill-suited to the players at his disposal.

Things like leadership and communication skills. We can cut Pocognoli some slack in that English is not his first language. He comes across as a thoroughly decent and likeable chap. He’s doing his best. He wants to embrace the culture and makes an effort to sing the National Anthem.

Scotland's defeat arose from individual mistakes, a common theme during the Belgian's reign.

All of that is undoubtedly to be welcomed. Good on him. But would anyone describe him as an inspirational figure?

When you listen to him speak, have you ever felt slightly confused in terms of the message he’s actually trying to get across?

In a recent development, how must that sound in the dressing room? When Andy Robertson spoke post-match on Monday night, there was frustration in his voice.

According to recent reports, the captain insisted there is simply no time or patience with these things. Scotland need to deliver results now.

To be fair, there actually would be a degree of patience shown by the Tartan Army towards Pocognoli if there was something to actually believe in.

There was a lot of goodwill towards him at the start. If there were signs across these last six games that he could deliver a more exciting team to watch, they would show patience.

But on the basis of what we’ve seen so far, there’s been absolutely nothing to suggest he can move this team forward. Ask yourself a very simple question – do Scotland pass the eye test?

Are we seeing a team who are playing on the front foot and creating chances? The answer, obviously, is no.

Sources indicate that steve Clarke celebrates Scotland's win over Denmark a year ago... how fans miss such highs.

Many Scotland fans are now confronting the possibility that we might not even qualify for Euro 2028, a tournament which we are co-hosting.

By finishing third in the Nations League, we will now be in pot three for the Euro qualifiers and will face a more difficult group.

Beyond that, we would be relying on the back-door method of one of the best-placed home nations not to qualify directly.

Recent findings suggest that those Euro qualifiers will start in March of next year. Does Pocognoli even make it that far? Or should the SFA hold their hands up, admit they’ve made a mistake, and rectify it?

That feels unlikely. But on the basis of what we have seen over these first six games, it’s hard to see how this gets any better.

Sources indicate that we are worse now than we were at the end under Clarke. Much, much worse. This is not teething problems. It’s a team who have regressed massively under a head coach who was supposed to move the whole thing forward.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Malik Tillman has admitted that recent criticism from the club’s supporters has diminished his appreciation of their applause. Speaking after Saturday’s 4-0 Bundesliga victory over SC Paderborn, the 24-year-old former Germany U21 and current USMNT international offered a remarkably candid assessment of his relationship with the Leverkusen faithful despite producing his best performance of the season.

Tillman assisted Afonso Moreira’s opening goal with an excellent pass and impressed with several further attacking contributions. When head coach Carles Martínez substituted the midfielder in the 67th minute, the BayArena crowd responded with enthusiastic applause and chants of his name.

Industry observers note that the reception contrasted sharply with Leverkusen’s recent 4-2 home defeat against VfB Stuttgart, when Tillman was greeted by boos upon entering the pitch as a substitute. Rather than welcome the change in attitude, however, the former Bayern Munich academy player suggested that such reactions no longer carried much significance for him.

Get German Football News previously reported on Tillman’s frustrations with Leverkusen supporters following a revealing interview with the Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger in August. The American acknowledged that criticism of his performances was sometimes justified, but emphasized that some reactions had become excessively personal. Tillman also discussed difficulties with former coach Kasper Hjulmand and expressed disappointment over the support he had received from the club’s management.

The midfielder arrived from PSV Eindhoven in the summer of 2025 for approximately €35 million. The considerable expectations accompanying his arrival have frequently proven difficult to fulfill. Our detailed preseason assessment of Leverkusen highlighted Tillman’s difficulties establishing himself in Martínez’s plans amid increased competition for attacking positions.

According to recent reports, saturday’s performance nevertheless offered fresh encouragement. Tillman demonstrated the technical quality and creativity that persuaded Leverkusen to invest heavily in his services. Whether the latest display will help repair his relationship with sections of the club’s support remains another matter.

“I have confidence in myself, but playing a good game naturally strengthens that confidence even further,” Tillman explained after Saturday’s match, as reported by Kicker. “I have to keep going here, no matter what happens. But I’m happy with my performance.”.

Asked how he felt about receiving applause after previously being booed, the American offered a notably different response.

“It’s difficult to say at this point,” Tillman admitted. “I don’t really care anymore. I don’t know. Of course, it sucks when you get booed, and at the end of the day, it doesn’t really mean much to me anymore when people cheer or shout my name.”.

  • According to recent reports, baum, already dealing with a banged-up defensive corps, had to contend with more bad news this week in the form of injuries to central defenders Chrislain Matsima and Jeffrey Gouweleeuw.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A Bundesliga battle between two teams desperate to snap poor runs of form ended in favor of the Bavarian Swabian hosts. Two matchdays into the current Bundesliga campaign, Manuel Baum’s Augsburg were celebrating their status as the top team in the table. Unfortunately, Baum’s Fuggerstädter then proceeded to go seven league fixtures without a win. That streak is now history following a 3-1 home win over Mainz.

The hosts entered Sunday’s encounter hovering just above the relegation zone, three places below Urs Fischer’s Mainz. Fischer’s team nevertheless only possessed one point more and counted as one of the biggest disappointments of the German top flight. The Rheinhessen traveled to Bavaria on a four-match losing streak, including a loss to 2. Bundesliga outfit Bochum that dumped them out of the Pokal in the second round.

According to recent reports, baum, already dealing with a banged-up defensive corps, had to contend with more bad news this week in the form of injuries to central defenders Chrislain Matsima and Jeffrey Gouweleeuw. Matsima’s absence forced the FCA trainer to hand 18-year-old prospect Tim Schnitzer his Bundesliga starting XI debut. Captain Gouweleeuw, meanwhile, could luckily enough be replaced by Manchester City loanee Juma Bah, who had returned from suspension. Schnitzer and Bah were among five changes to the starting XI Baum employed in the recent 5-2 away defeat to RB Leipzig. Marius Wolf, Michael Gregoritsch, and Alexis Claude-Maurice started over Han-Noah Massengo, Arijon Ibrahimovic, and Rodrigo Ribeiro.

Fischer too needed to pull the trigger on several changes. Though the Mainz trainer declared himself largely satisfied with the performance of his team in a narrow loss against Bayern Munich just prior to the international break, four fresh outfielders took to the pitch for the Rheinhessen. Fischer, having several of his preferred starters back, sent Phillip Tietz, Phillipp Mwene, Paul Nebel, and Stefan Posch onto the field in place of Ransford Königsdörffer, Silvan Widmer, Jae-Sung Lee, and Fabio Gruber. Posch returned from suspension after getting sent off in a disastrous encounter against Elversberg that saw Fischer’s charges dispatched 4-1.

Baum’s changes certainly produced attractive football in the opening stages. Wolf’s placement as the right wingback enabled the reliably versatile Robin Fellhauer to slide inside and work in the packed midfield alongside Fabian Rieder, Claude-Maurice, and Anton Kade. This particular FCA foursome strode forward with reckless abandon, mostly keeping Mainz pinned back in their own half throughout the entire first quarter-of-an-hour. Sharp combos involving the midfield and the wingbacks produced plenty of incursions into the FSV penalty area. Kade unfortunately couldn’t find the right angle on the best of the opportunities to score, shooting well wide from only six meters out in the 12th minute.

Industry observers note that the opener finally came on Augsburg’s second corner of the afternoon. A quality free-kick from Claude-Maurice was actually shepherded out into touch deftly by former FCA striker Phillip Tietz in the 19th minute. Newly minted FCA record holder Gregoritsch was able to convert the subsequent set-piece for the 1-0. Makeshift Augsburg defender Yannik Keitel did an excellent job beating Mainz’s Kaishu Sano in an aerial duel after Rieder swung in the corner from the right. Keitel’s header was initially saved by Robin Zentner, who parried the ball toward the far post. The rebound fell perfectly for the onrushing Gregoritsch, who easily slid in his sixth Bundesliga goal of the campaign. As Baum and his crew knew full well, however, an early lead meant little.

In their ongoing seven-game winless run, Augsburg had actually squandered the lead in six of them. On five occasions, Baum’s team scored the opening goal of the match. Some five minutes after Gregoritsch opened the scoring, it appeared as if another lead was almost certain to evaporate. Somehow, one of Mainz’s most dependable scorers spurned a chance to equalize. Tietz found himself free in front of goal in the 24th off a blitz counter, but blasted the ball well over the bar in front of his former FanKurve. Apart from that chance, the Bavarian Swabian hosts did still remain the more active side.

Recent findings suggest that the 2-0 finally came off yet another corner from the right in the 36th minute. This time, fellow fresh starter Bah would bundle home another Rieder corner when Mainz couldn’t get the service from the right clear. Amid all the jostling prior to Bah bundling the ball home, the second goal withstood VAR scrutiny. Regrettably, the rest of the half would fall prey to officiating controversies. A sequence of events shortly after the second goal quickly led to match official Martin Petersen losing control of the match.

According to recent reports, augsburg thought they had scored the 3-0 in the 41st minute when Keitel slotted home off a quick throw-in. Petersen nevertheless ruled that FCA defender Bah had fouled Mainz counterpart Kacper Potulski in the lead-up. Petersen highlighted restraint by not booking the crowd of Augsburg players who stood before him to protest his decision, but offered head coach Baum no such quarter when he kept Nadiem Amiri from executing a throw-in in the 43rd. Baum kept the ball himself whilst protesting to Petersen. The FCA trainer was promptly ejected from proceedings on a straight red.

Petersen found himself at the center of more protests from players before it was time to head into the tunnel. The hosts were not pleased when the referee declined to whistle for a shove by Posch on Claude-Maurice just outside the box during first-half injury time. Prior to that, Petersen was compelled by VAR to take another look at a Fellhauer foul on Sano in the 44th. Petersen initially only awarded a yellow card despite the fact that Fellhauer caught Sano on the knee with his swinging boot. Petersen stood by his decision and was surely pleased to retreat to the tunnel after a heated, scrappy, and contentious end to the half.

To the relief of most observers, the focus returned to football after the change of ends. There would be no controversy attached to either of the goals scored in the opening five minutes of the second half. The hosts added their third goal shortly after play resumed. A free-kick delivery from the right was initially cleared before Behrens headed the ball back into the penalty area. Wolf helped it onward, and Posch inadvertently glanced the ball into Gregoritsch’s path in the 48th minute. The Austrian striker stroked home the 3-0. Fischer’s team responded by pulling a goal back promptly, with halftime sub Königsdörffer polishing off a nice distance effort on a quick counter three minutes later.

Königsdörffer’s 3-1 worked wonders for the carnival club’s confidence, and Fischer’s men undeniably looked more assured heading forward for the duration of proceedings. Mainz tightened up the possession statistics and looked more inspired when forging ahead. The more optically pleasing football from Mainz nevertheless didn’t end up producing another goal or even another memorable attempt on target. Instead, it was Augsburg who looked more dangerous on the counter. FCA sub Uchenna Ogundu unluckily missed out on the 4-1 with a strike off the inside of the far post in the 81st.

Finn Dahmen (5) – Juma Bah (6), Yannik Keitel (6), Tim Schnitzer (6) – Marius Wolf (6), Robin Fellhauer (6), Fabian Rieder (6), Hennes Behrens (5) – Anton Kade (6), Alexis Claude-Maurice (5) – Michael Gregoritsch (7).

Substitutes: Arijon Ibrahimovic (6), Uchenna Ogundu (6), Young-Woo Seol (-), Mert Kömür (-).

Robin Zentner (4) – Danny da Costa (5), Stefan Posch (1), Kacper Potulski (6), Anthony Caci (5) – Kaishu Sano (5), Phillipp Mwene (6) – Paul Nebel (4), Nadiem Amiri (3), Sheraldo Becker (4) – Phillip Tietz (4).

Substitutes: Ransford Königsdörffer (7), Benedict Hollerbach (6), Silvan Widmer (6), Eric Martel (-), Rael Nakuzola (-).

The Austrian international proved the difference-maker with an exceptionally efficient performance in front of goal. Gregoritsch scored twice from just three shots, putting both of his efforts on target past Robin Zentner and outperforming his 1.36 xG. The 31-year-old wasn’t particularly involved in Augsburg’s build-up play, registering just 26 touches and completing 56 percent of his passes during his 72 minutes on the pitch. Gregoritsch nevertheless demonstrated precisely why Baum continues to place his faith in him. The veteran striker’s opportunistic finishing on both goals helped Augsburg snap their seven-match winless streak and lifted his Bundesliga tally to six goals for the season.

GGFN | Peter Weis – reporting from the WWK Arena.

Man United Confidential: Mauricio Pochettino to be given money to spend in January as club target recruits in THREE positions - and surprise at popular coach's sacking

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino’s whirlwind arrival as Manchester United’s new head coach has left little time to work out where he will live – but a key factor in that decision will be his beloved dog Sansa.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 17 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino’s whirlwind arrival as Manchester United’s new head coach has left little time to work out where he will live – but a key factor in that decision will be his beloved dog Sansa.

Pochettino will leave the TQL Stadium in Cincinnati after the USA’s game against Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning and go straight to the airport to catch an eight-hour flight to Manchester on board a private jet paid for by United.

The club will also provide him with somewhere to live as he settles into the new job and finds a more permanent residence.

The 54-year-old, who also has a home in Barcelona, is said to have lived just outside London when he was Tottenham manager and then spent the entirety of his 18-month spell as Paris Saint-Germain boss in a luxury hotel.

Pochettino lived in Knightsbridge while he was in charge of Chelsea, and revealed that he enjoyed getting feedback from fans while out on his daily 90-minute dog walks with Sansa.

He named the Rhodesian Ridgeback after a character from Game of Thrones and has even given the dog her own Instagram account.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of the US national team for the final time in the early hours of Wednesday morning, then head straight to Manchester on a private jet.

Pochettino (pictured with his son Maurizio) will have to find accommodation which suits his dog Sansa, a Rhodesian Ridgeback (Source: Instagram/pochettino).

Describing the difficulty of Spurs playing on a Saturday night in 2018, he stated: ‘At 7pm, I am normally on my sofa with my dog Sansa watching the Spanish league because they start at 7.45pm, or France because Ligue 1 starts at 8pm, or Italy, or different games.

‘It will be so strange for my dog. Not for me but my dog. “Where is my dad?” she is going to say. She is beautiful and I am in love with her.’.

The living habits of United bosses have varied over the years. Sir Alex Ferguson, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ruben Amorim favoured Wilmslow and Alderley Edge, David Moyes remained further afield in Lytham, Louis van Gaal and Erik ten Hag chose Hale, and Jose Mourinho famously spent 895 days at the Lowry Hotel in Manchester (where dogs can stay for an additional £30).

United have no plans to change the timings for Wednesday’s training session, even though Pochettino and four of his backroom team may not arrive at Carrington until the early afternoon.

The private jet carrying the Argentine, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott should touch down from Cincinnati around noon.

An advance party of three more coaches – Pochettino’s assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino – have been in Manchester since Sunday after they were released early by the US Soccer Federation as a gesture of goodwill following the 6-0 first-leg win over Haiti in the quarter-finals of the North American equivalent of the Nations League.

They took training on Tuesday as United’s players continue to report back from international duty, and will also oversee the session on Wednesday morning after United decided not to reschedule it so Pochettino could be present.

The Argentine will be firmly hands-on from Thursday, though, as he prepares for his first game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Pochettino, who will speak to club media shortly after his arrival before conducting his first press conference on Friday, has faced Liverpool 19 times in his managerial career, losing 11 games, drawing five and winning three.

Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez (right) has been in Manchester since Sunday and took training on Tuesday.

Strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya - the first woman to be part of United's backroom staff - will travel with Pochettino to Manchester following the Haiti game.

Pochettino will inherit a team in the relegation zone – which could even be bottom of the Premier League by kick-off on Sunday – and it’s understood he will be given modest funds to improve his squad in the January transfer window.

United are in desperate need of a left back and a striker, having failed to sign cover in both positions in the summer.

One potential target may be US centre forward Folarin Balogun who has prospered under Pochettino but only started once for Monaco this season after a summer move to Everton fell through. United sources say the newly introduced head coach will have input in the weeks ahead before a clearer plan emerges.

United also want a centre back after Confidential revealed last week that Fulham’s Calvin Bassey and Nathan Collins, of Brentford, are two options being considered.

It’s possible that one of those deals may have to be a loan, however, with United’s delicate financial situation set to be spelt out in black and white when the results from the first quarter of the financial year are released on Thursday.

Although Pochettino is going to have money for new players, United will have to be smart in their transfer dealings and spend wisely.

In the short term, Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford may be available again for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool.

However, there is a concern over Patrick Dorgu who was deemed to be unfit for international duty with Denmark, even though he returned to action for Michael Carrick’s final game after a month-and-a-half out with a hamstring injury and headed a stoppage-time equaliser in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Fulham's Calvin Bassey (right) is among the centre-back options United are considering.

Marcus Rashford may be available for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool.

It was the departure of Travis Binnion, rather than Carrick, that raised the most eyebrows among figures working in football over the past few days.

Agents and first-team players privately described their surprise at seeing Binnion – a long-time academy figure before stepping up to the first team to help Darren Fletcher as interim and then Carrick – leave the club.

United have cleaned house for the arrival of Pochettino’s backroom team, and Binnion was one of those who paid the price.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who are known to have enjoyed working with Binnion.

Despite stepping up to the first team, where he would watch matches from the press box alongside United’s team of analysts, Binnion remained in contact with numerous academy player representatives to ensure their development was progressing as planned.

Binnion, who first arrived in 2019 as an Under 16s coach and progressed to the Under 18s, Under 21s and then head of player development and coaching, isn’t expected to be out of the game for too long though.

Agency sources believe rival Premier League academies will move quickly to recruit him, with Everton seen as one potential landing spot. United’s former academy head Nick Cox is now Everton technical director and has already recruited Dave Hughes and Tom Curtis, who worked under Binnion at United.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who enjoyed working with Travis Binnion (pictured).

Your responses to our 36-man Manchester United squad audit have made for interesting reading over the last week.

Confidential pored over the first-team squad, as well as numerous rising stars in the academy, that Pochettino and his staff will quickly have to run the rule over.

While some of the voting went as expected – your votes demonstrated an overwhelming desire among the fanbase to see Noussair Mazraoui, Diogo Dalot, Shaw and Harry Maguire leave this summer – there were a few surprises.

Many voted for captain Bruno Fernandes, who just recently rejected a second contract extension offer, to be moved on, along with Rashford. Amad Diallo and summer signing Andrey Santos are two who divide opinion, but both made the cut.

Check out the full squad audit HERE to see how others voted and leave your own verdict!

Confidential understands JJ Gabriel’s representatives held fresh talks with Real Madrid at the club’s training ground on Monday as a move to the Santiago Bernabeu edges ever closer.

Now that Gabriel has officially announced a partnership with Epic Sports Agency, his agent Ali Barat is leading negotiations and has been at Real’s Valdebebas headquarters along with the 16-year-old and his family.

Gabriel confirmed his departure from the club in an Instagram video on Tuesday night, as he and the Spanish giants hope to get a move over the line.

JJ Gabriel's representatives have held fresh talks with Real Madrid as his move to the Bernabeu edges closer.

Eric Cantona and Sir Alex Ferguson will reunite next month at a special screening of the Frenchman’s new documentary.

Cantona: Flower of Evil won rave reviews in France and is now heading to the UK, with a one-night-only panel featuring Cantona and Ferguson at Aviva Studios in Manchester on December 7.

Recent findings suggest that the documentary film digs deeper into how Ferguson channelled Cantona’s brilliance and honed his explosiveness – a trait that had seen him branded ‘unmanageable’ in France. Tickets range from £156 all the way up to £1,000. You can purchase them here.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Sources indicate that alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

In a recent development, palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was confirmed Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”.

Industry observers note that "Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

It has been revealed that palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

It looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Industry observers note that cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

It has been revealed that “Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, mentioned. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”.

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

Reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.
